original_test_intent: Inject a fatal SWA rail error for every required DDR5 PMIC/DIMM and voltage type, verify the intended immediate reset and fresh SWA-specific persistent evidence, then prove voltage, temperature, memory and I2C management recovery before the next target.
original_method: Map every DIMM to socket/die/UMC/channel/slot, PMIC address and BMC/platform I2C controller/bus; prove railtype0=SWA and voltagetype0/1 meanings; approve a syntactically valid tuple per run; capture electrical/log baseline; inject one target under OOB capture; decode fresh PMIC/CPER/SEL evidence; validate reset/boot, rail telemetry, memory training and workload; restore settings and re-enable telemetry before any next run.
manual_activity: The FAE and platform/BMC owner map every PMIC target, approve SWA/voltage semantics and electrical limits, execute one fatal injection at a time, recover memory power and restore PMIC/I2C settings.
required_inputs: Populated DIMM-to-socket/die/UMC/channel/slot/PMIC-address map and complete per-run tuple matrix
Wistron BMC/platform I2C controller/bus/address/OOB path and expected response for each PMIC
Vendor proof railtype0 is SWA and definitions/expected signatures for voltagetype0 and 1
Correct command-line continuation plus approved socketdieumc/dimm value for every target
PMIC rail voltage/current/temperature safe envelope, hard aborts and fatal/reset behavior
Fresh PMIC/CPER/BERT/SEL fields, reset/boot deadlines, memory-training/workload recovery and full restoration
safety_requirements: Dedicated instrumented DDR5 SUT with independent BMC/serial access and approved PMIC recovery
Record raw BIOS, PMIC telemetry, I2C ownership, DIMM SPD/topology and error baseline without erasing evidence
Inject one DIMM/voltage tuple once; measure rail and temperature and require full memory recovery before another
Abort on mapping mismatch, out-of-envelope voltage/current/temperature, unexpected reset, boot/training failure, missing DIMM, stale evidence or I2C loss
No automatic sequence/retry; restore PMIC mode, fault recovery, SPD host control, telemetry, I2C enables and HDT state
agent_execution_scope: Validate SWA encoding, topology, I2C ownership, per-target tuple, electrical envelope, evidence and recovery plan
Collect read-only PMIC/I2C identity, telemetry, raw settings, OOB/BERT/CPER/SEL, DIMM enumeration and memory-health evidence
Do not infer targets/addresses/rails, change BIOS/HDT/I2C, inject, reset, repeat, recover or decide verdict
engineer_actions: Approve per-DIMM SWA/voltage matrix and I2C ownership
Approve electrical aborts, fatal evidence and memory recovery
Supervise each isolated injection and reset
Restore all PMIC/I2C settings and issue per-run verdict

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: Generic PMIC keyword logs cannot distinguish SWA/railtype0, voltagetype, physical DIMM or a fresh fatal event, and provide no electrical recovery proof.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: After per-DIMM PMIC/I2C mapping and SWA encoding approval, run one vendor-correct tuple under OOB and telemetry capture, validate persistent source evidence and memory recovery, then separately authorize another voltage or DIMM.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: listvalidumc, socketdieumc0:0:3, railtype0, voltagetype0/1, dimm0, immediate reset, all-DIMM instruction, PMIC/I2C BIOS settings and 360/120-minute values remain preserved as gated inputs.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Execute a serialized, instrumented SWA fatal matrix with one mapped PMIC target per run, fresh durable attribution and complete electrical/memory rollback.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds BMC/I2C ownership, PMIC address mapping, command parsing, explicit target matrix, electrical limits, durable fields and per-run memory validation.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: One fixed tuple cannot cover all DIMMs/voltage types, and tool PASS cannot prove the correct rail or safe recovery.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Incorrect rail or PMIC selection can cause destructive voltage behavior, persistent DIMM loss, boot failure or unavailable management access.

project_override_considerations: I2C is BMC/platform-management scope by project rule. Linux-visible buses alone cannot prove the PMIC target. Preserve the source's all-DIMM/two-voltage scope even if the platform matrix marks some combinations not applicable; do not silently reduce coverage.
expected_evidence: Complete DIMM/UMC/PMIC/I2C controller-bus-address and SWA/voltage tuple matrix
Pinned tool/spec plus raw BIOS, PMIC telemetry, SPD and memory baseline
One exact command and OOB reset/firmware/boot timeline per authorized tuple
Fresh SWA-specific PMIC status, CPER/BERT/SEL source/severity and reset-cause record
In-envelope rail/thermal recovery, complete DIMM enumeration/training and bounded memory workload
Per-run restoration diff and engineer verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: The source requires every DIMM and voltage type0/1 but provides only fixed 0:0:3/dimm0/voltagetype0 and no expansion algorithm. The displayed command is split without explicit continuation. Railtype0-to-SWA and I2C/PMIC target ownership are unproven, while electrical and timing acceptance is absent.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The fatal SWA PMIC purpose and literal seed tuple are identifiable. Engineering can supply the target matrix and electrical contract, so static review completes while execution stays gated.

engineering_decision_pending.question: Resolve Reliability row 88 Wistron-System RAS-00808-V002: prove railtype0=SWA and define voltagetype0/1; provide every populated DIMM's socket/die/UMC/channel/slot/dimm plus PMIC address and Wistron BMC/platform I2C controller/bus/OOB mapping; approve command continuation and full tuple matrix; specify electrical limits, fatal PMIC/CPER/BERT/SEL evidence, reset/boot deadlines, memory-training/workload recovery, aborts and restoration of PMIC/I2C/HDT settings.

review_improvement: Adds a physically traceable SWA rail matrix, Wistron I2C ownership, electrical safeguards and per-DIMM recovery instead of treating a fixed tuple as all-DIMM coverage.
independent_technical_reasoning: A PMIC fatal injection changes the memory power domain, so the decisive facts are the physical DIMM/PMIC address and actual rail response, not a generic log keyword. The source's hard-coded UMC and dimm0 cannot enumerate every DIMM, and two voltage types may exercise distinct fault comparators. Because I2C ownership is platform management scope, target identity and recovery must be proven through the approved controller path before any rail fault is armed.
